topic: The Mystery of Pi: Definition and History

sections.title: The Hook: The Constant Ratio
lecture_lines: Circles of all sizes share a secret ratio.
Small hamster wheels, large Ferris wheels alike.
This special ratio is always the same.
animations: Draw diameter d (#00FF00) and show equation d = 2r.
Highlight the constant ratio d/r = 2 near the shape.

sections.title: Defining Pi (π)
lecture_lines: Pi is circumference divided by diameter.
Unwind the string around the circle.
It takes three lengths plus a remainder.
animations: Show circumference C (#FFFF00) tracing around circle.
Animate unrolling C into a straight line segment.

sections.title: Historical Evolution: From Estimation to Precision
lecture_lines: Archimedes used polygons to trap circles.
More sides mean a better estimate.
animations: Show ancient approximations (3 or 3.125) as #CCCCCC text.
Animate Archimedes' polygon (n=6) surrounding a circle.
Increase n to 12, 24, showing convergence toward circle.

sections.title: The Irrational Nature of Pi
lecture_lines: It never ends and never repeats.
Computers can never find its end.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Relevance
lecture_lines: Pi bridges linear and curved geometry.
Vital for GPS and space travel.
animations: Draw an engineering arch with circular curvature.
Overlay space/satellite trajectory calculation formula involving π.
Flash π in #00FF00 to signify universal constant.
